correctness.rationale: For every N>=3 and K>0, linearization is K diag(c)L. AB/BA identifies all nonzero eigenvalues with those of the real symmetric H^(1/2)diag(c)H^(1/2); Sylvester inertia on the mean-zero space gives necessary-and-sufficient stability. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz proves the exact one-negative-cosine threshold and handles zero cases. The impurity curvature is realized by solving L phi=q, the force-balance equation is F_n(t)=Delta/K; strict F_n″<0 gives a unique nondegenerate fold and stable/unstable sides. A direct Taylor expansion proves the leading width. Standalone VERIFY.py passed 16900 random signed-form tests across N=3,...,15 and actual locked-state and fold tests; finite testing is not used to replace analytical quantifiers. At fold zero has algebraic multiplicity two in full phase coordinates; nonlinear stability there is unproved.

value.rationale: The actual primary dynamics raises a natural open-in-main-text question about nonprincipal sine-inverse branches. A sharp all-N stability criterion demonstrates that one negative cosine need not destabilize and identifies a nonempty one-impurity branch whose fold is exactly located. The positive mixed-curvature window shrinks at a sharp order K/(2(N−1)^2), showing precisely how this neglected locking type persists but becomes hard to see for large rings. This is a physically interpretable bifurcation boundary for a natural frequency impurity, rather than an arbitrary tabulated finite slice. Global existence among all branches and nonlinear fold dynamics remain unproved.
